bugs.summary: Vcells count drops, or wraps past zero, after a symbol lookup through a differently marked copy of its name
bugs.creator: r

comments.text:
Looking up an existing symbol through a copy of its name with another declared encoding leaves the copy hashed, and freeing it lowers the vector heap count by the hash. R 4.5.3 and R Under development (unstable) (2026-09-30 r90605), x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, en_US.UTF-8:

    $ R --vanilla --quiet
    > vcells <- function() { invisible(gc()); gc()["Vcells", c("used", "gc trigger")] }
    > x <- strrep("\u00e9", 100L)   # 200 bytes, declared UTF-8
    > s <- as.symbol(x)             # makes the symbol, named by x
    > vcells()
          used gc trigger
        528900    8388608
    > local({ y <- x; Encoding(y) <- "unknown"; invisible(as.symbol(y)) })
    > vcells()
            used   gc trigger
    1.844674e+19 1.844674e+19

In a fresh session, a name refused for its length wraps the used count the same way: try(as.symbol(strrep("a", 10001L))).

The shortfall persists, adds up with each such copy freed, and is not just a reporting error: the same count decides when an allocation triggers a collection, how the heap is resized, as the gc trigger above shows, and when the vector limit is reached (src/main/memory.c:2710-2714, 1184).

The root cause is installNoTrChar() storing the hash in the CHARSXP's TRUELENGTH (src/main/names.c:1303-1306) before returning an existing symbol named by a different CHARSXP (or refusing a name over MAXIDSIZE). Either way the CHARSXP stays hashed without becoming a PRINTNAME. On a CHARSXP, CACHED_MASK is the bit GROWABLE_MASK tests (src/include/Defn.h:937-938), so once it is collected, getVecSizeInVEC() sizes it by TRUELENGTH and the hash is what comes off R_LargeVallocSize (memory.c:1108-1109, 1166). Only CHARSXPs in the large-vector class are affected.

Would it be worth leaving CHARSXPs out of the growable adjustment in getVecSizeInVEC(), since bit 5 means cached on them? Storing the hash only once installNoTrChar() makes the CHARSXP a PRINTNAME would also close both cases. I'm happy to supply a patch if this sounds right.

Disclosure: I used an AI assistant to find the cause in the R sources and to draft this report, then edited it and reproduced the results myself on R 4.5.3 and R-devel r90605.

comments.text:
Created attachment 3882
No longer apply the growable adjustment to CHARSXPs in getVecSizeInVEC() and store the hash only once the CHARSXP has become a PRINTNAME in installNoTrChar()

Patch against trunk r90605, in three parts: getVecSizeInVEC() no longer applies the growable adjustment to CHARSXPs, installNoTrChar() stores the hash only once the CHARSXP has become a PRINTNAME, and tests/reg-tests-1e.R gains two regression tests. The first checks that the Vcells count neither falls nor wraps; it fails on stock r90605 and passes with either change alone. The second reads the hash bit through .Internal(inspect()), with a symbol’s own name as a positive control, and fails without the installNoTrChar() change. With both changes, both tests pass in a normal build and in one configured with –enable-strict-barrier. The full make check passes with each change alone and with both, and repeating the lookup and the refused name 400 times leaves no drift in the count.

OSS-Fuzz ran into this through unserialize(): a SYMSXP whose name is longer than 10000 bytes takes the refused-name path, so reading serialized data is enough to wrap the count. The fuzzing process, started with R_MAX_VSIZE=512Mb, then stopped collecting on vector allocation and grew to 2.5 Gb (testcase 4823638474555392).

I arrived at the same getVecSizeInVEC() change as attachment 3882 before finding this report, and can confirm it on trunk r90874: with that hunk alone the count is unchanged in both cases and the limit holds again. That hunk, with a test in tests/reg-fuzz.R, is at https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/466, where CI results can be seen.
